Merge Risk: ⚪ Minimal · up to 01f02
The search changes are mergeable after normal checks; the examined indexing and access paths revealed no actionable blocker.
Security architecture risk: 🔵 Low · up to 01f02
The change tightens access to private item context while preserving existing search access checks. No introduced authorization bypass was identified. The backfill requeues every non-deleted item, but production rollout capacity and recovery procedures were not verified. **Retained concerns** No architecture-level concerns identified.
Security review details
**Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — The changed security outcome concerns parent-item metadata exposed through authenticated search, including documents shared out of private items. It narrows that exposure without granting new item privileges. The separate indexing backfill spans all non-deleted items rather than a single workspace. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — Session authentication supplies the user identity. Db::begin_as sets transaction-local app.user_id, and visible_items uses that transaction rather than a privileged indexing connection. The items SELECT policy requires app_item_access to succeed; fallback also checks that function before returning parent-item IDs. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _observed_ — The existing queue protocol retains ownership and generation checks. Successful asynchronous work deletes a row only when its current queued_at matches the submitted generation; a refresh with a different timestamp survives completion of older work. Failed work remains queued for retry. The PR changes enqueue coverage, not this settlement protocol.
